openings.claim: Replace strap-only retention with two removable opposite-side padded jaws: upper/lower aluminum-strip pairs bolted outside hatch/trough could resist slip and distribute compression. Capture pads without adhesive; mark placement and tighten alternately, avoiding isolated left-corner loading. Remove assemblies completely for inspection; cord-loop bolts, nuts and pads together and recover beside fixture.
openings.discriminator: Against strap-only friction retention, jaws should reduce displacement without opposite-corner lift; unmeasured, and straps could perform equally well. Success requires position error <=1 mm after ten openings, resistance to 20 N, reopening <=30 seconds, and no new visible seal tears, including final right-contact 1 mm card disturbance; only seal-contact continuity is exempt.
openings.probe: First ruler-check loose strips for straddling hatch/rim, with every bolt outside existing material and no permanent deformation. If feasible, drill only strips and fabricate within 90 minutes. Run ten opening/closure/pull cycles within 20 observation minutes; place supplied card at marked right contact on final closure. Record position, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal condition each cycle; stop on damage or inability to seat. One configuration consumes ten of twelve trials. This tests outcome feasibility, not superiority over the untested strap rival.
openings.uncertainty: Accessible underside and outboard bolt clearance are indispensable and unprovided. Four strips/six bolts must form two jaws without additional carriers; rubber friction, strip stiffness and seal-safe force are unknown. Defeated by jaw slip, card-induced rocking, opposite-corner lift, damage, fabrication overrun or reopening >30 seconds.

lineage.reason: Retains causal change, rival, complete outcomes, disturbance, probe limits, stopping conditions, uncertainties and declared uncertain fit.

decision: Bounded candidate probe. Preserve existing hatch/rim/seal; do not drill, cut, glue or permanently deform hatch/trough. Keep full marked opening unobstructed when open, use no powered mechanism, recover loose components. Geometry failure establishes no feasible joint; unknown resources authorize no constraint relaxation or alteration to rescue it.
